draft.title: Chromatography
card: Chromatography separates substances that are dissolved together, such as the different dyes in a black ink. It works on a mixture that has been dissolved in a liquid.
A spot of the mixture is placed near the bottom of a strip of chromatography paper. The bottom edge of the paper is then stood in a solvent, with the spot kept above the solvent level.
The solvent soaks up the paper and carries the substances in the spot with it. Each substance travels a different distance, so the substances end up as separate spots at different heights.
A substance that moves a long way is carried easily by the solvent. A substance that moves only a short way is carried less easily. If an ink leaves two spots, it contains at least two dyes.
draft.remember: Chromatography separates dissolved substances because each one travels a different distance up the paper.

a.q: Why does chromatography separate the dyes in a black ink?
opts: Each dye travels a different distance up the paper
Each dye dissolves in the paper at a different speed
The paper catches the dyes that are not dissolved
The solvent boils off and leaves each dye behind
a.why: The solvent carries the dyes up the paper, and each dye travels a different distance, so they end up apart. Catching undissolved solids is filtration, and the dyes in ink are already dissolved.
a.clue: Think about what the solvent does as it moves up the paper.

b.q: Ravi tests a green felt-tip pen with chromatography. The result shows a blue spot and a yellow spot at different heights. What does this tell him about the green ink?
opts: It is a mixture of at least two dyes
It is a pure substance with one dye
It is a solvent that has not moved
b.why: Two spots at different heights mean two substances travelled different distances. So the ink is a mixture of at least two dyes. A pure substance would leave only one spot.
b.clue: Count the spots left on the paper.

wants.brief: A strip of chromatography paper standing in a beaker with the bottom edge in the solvent. The starting spot is above the solvent level. After the run, three spots of different colours sit at different heights above the start line. Labels: paper, solvent, start spot, separated spots.
wants.why: It shows how the set-up works and how the dyes end up at different heights.

a.best: Each dye travels a different distance up the paper

b.best: It is a mixture of at least two dyes
